coverage.evidence: 'react-hooks/set-state-in-effect is enabled and use-media-query.ts fails if its setState-in-effect shape returns.' Enabled: eslint --print-config on quick-add.tsx reports 16 react-hooks rules in effect with set-state-in-effect at severity 2. Fails if it returns: the old implementation was restored verbatim and lint reported 'error Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders ... react-hooks/set-state-in-effect' at its line, then the file was restored and lints clean. This is the criterion the whole item exists for, because that repair could be guarded by nothing else.

'quick-add.tsx's reset-on-open no longer calls setState inside an effect, and Quick Add still starts empty every time so nothing is recorded twice.' Both halves. The effect is gone and lint passes with set-state-in-effect at error. The behaviour is held by quick-add.test.tsx:277, which opens the sheet, types 2000, picks a category, saves, reopens and asserts the amount field is empty — and it passes. Proven able to fail: removing the key from app-shell fails that case and only that case, 1 failed and 7 passed.

'plan-screen.tsx passes preserve-manual-memoization and the React Compiler no longer skips optimising the component.' The useMemo is removed and lint reports no react-hooks error on the file with all sixteen rules enabled; the compiler's own message, 'Compilation Skipped: Existing memoization could not be preserved', no longer appears. Checked why rather than only that: carriedInLookup returns a closure without doing work, so the memo saved nothing, and cycle comes from cycleAt, a fresh object each render, so its dependency array never matched — the memo recomputed every render while costing the component its optimisation.

'Each rule newly enabled has been seen failing once on purpose.' Both rules that have anything to fail on were: set-state-in-effect by restoring use-media-query's old effect, and the money-safety behaviour behind the quick-add fix by removing app-shell's key. The remaining fourteen rules in the set report nothing on this codebase, so none can be made to fail without inventing a violation to prove a tool works — what was proven is that the set is in effect at error severity, which is the condition under which they would fail.

Nothing beyond the criteria. Four files: the config spread, the counter and its two call sites in app-shell, the effect removed from quick-add, the memo removed from plan-screen, plus two now-unused imports dropped rather than left behind. No feature, no screen, no behaviour the criteria did not ask for, and the two screens' line counts are untouched as work — they remain over REACT-03, which is ITEM-2's and is why that rule is deferred.

Each fix ships with the guard that would catch its regression, and the guards differ by what is guardable. quick-add's is a test, proven able to fail by removing the key. use-media-query's is the lint rule, proven able to fail by restoring the old shape — no test can guard it, because the repair preserved behaviour and its five tests pass against the old implementation. plan-screen's is the lint rule that reported it, for the same reason.

coverage.reason: No user journey is added or changed. The core journey in the addendum (K1) runs through Quick Add, and this item changes when its state is created rather than any step of it; the eight Quick Add cases and all 487 tests pass unchanged. That journey not existing as an end-to-end Playwright test is a standing project gap, neither created nor closable here.

coverage.evidence: The rule in scope — a sheet starts empty on every opening — is tested with the plain sequence a person performs, named for what it protects: 'starts empty each time, so nothing is recorded twice by accident'. Its neighbours cover the edges case by case: a rejected save keeps every value, changing the type drops a choice that no longer applies, a missing amount is refused, and the amount field holds focus on open.

The tests assert behaviour, and this refactor is the proof: the implementation of the reset changed completely, from an effect clearing four pieces of state to a remount, and not one test needed editing. A test coupled to the implementation would have had to change.

The abuse case on this screen is the money one, and it is the case under test: the sequence that would record the same amount twice is performed and refused. The input refusals themselves are unchanged and already covered.

Done twice, both ways round, before relying on either. Removing app-shell's key failed 'starts empty each time' and only that case. Restoring use-media-query's old effect raised the lint error. Both were restored and re-run green, 487 tests and lint 0 errors.

The tests import the real components by the specifiers the app uses, with no alias or build step between, so what vitest ran is what the bundle contains. CI's verify, which runs the same command, passes on this commit.

The edge this change is about is the second opening, and it is tested. The adjacent edges still pass unchanged: a rejected save keeps every value, the type change drops a stale choice, and focus lands on the amount field — the last being the one a remount could plausibly have broken, asserted through document.activeElement and passing.

summary: Pass. All four criteria hold and each was demonstrated by breaking something first: 16 rules in the computed config with set-state-in-effect at error, the old use-media-query shape now raising that error, and removing app-shell's key failing the money-safety test and only that one. The refactor needed no test edited, which is itself the evidence the tests check behaviour. Nothing extra built.
